items.body: Breton producer Quinquis (Emilie Quinquis) has announced “scenes d’interieur”, her original soundtrack to Melanie Leray’s stage production of the same name. The five-track release comes out on 13 November 2026 via Mute. The multi-media production blends theatre and film as it follows Chloe, an actress preparing to perform the role of Nora in Henrik Ibsen’s “A Doll’s House.” The stage sections trace the breakdown of Chloe’s own relationship, while a parallel story shown on film covers her childhood, raised by a mother who survived domestic violence. Ibsen’s 1879 play, which caused a scandal on release for questioning the traditional roles of men and women in marriage, runs through both timelines, tying the production to themes of control and the search for emancipation. Quinquis’ score follows the two timelines, underscoring Chloe’s vulnerability, pain and strength as she navigates the violence of her stepfather as a teenager and of her husband as an adult in the present day. She uses modular electronics to score the live theatre performances and acoustic instrumentation for the film sections, extending the dialogue between past and present that runs through the production. The single “Lena” is an intimate piece where slow-moving synths give way to distant voices as the track builds through layers of emotion. The album was recorded on Ushant Island, off the coast of Brittany, where Quinquis lives, and features a track recorded with Amsterdam-based labelmate Desire Marea, “Inkanuko.” “scenes d’interieur” (catalogue number iMUTE703) carries five tracks: “Chloe,” “Nora,” “Puzuilhan,” “Inkanuko” and “Lena.” It follows Quinquis’ 2025 album “eor” and the 2024 single “Morwreg”, both also released via Mute. About Quinquis Quinquis is the project of Breton producer Emilie Quinquis, based on Ushant Island off the coast of Brittany. Her work moves between electronic and acoustic instrumentation, built around modular synthesis, field recording and a close relationship to the Breton coast where she lives. Quinquis released the “aer” EP and the album “SEIM” before “Morwreg” preceded her 2025 album “eor,” both issued via Mute. “scenes d’interieur,” her soundtrack to Melanie Leray’s stage production of the same name, follows in November 2026 and marks her first release built specifically for a theatre production, combining her modular electronic work for the live stage sections with acoustic instrumentation for the production’s film sequences.

items._cn_summary: 布列塔尼制作人Quinquis为Melanie Leray的同名舞台剧创作了原声专辑，将剧场与影像两条时间线交织在一起。剧情围绕一位扮演易卜生《玩偶之家》中娜拉的演员展开，一面追溯她成年后婚姻关系的崩塌，一面通过影像呈现她童年与少年时期遭受家庭暴力的经历。音乐在两条叙事之间形成对照：现场剧场段落采用模块化电子设备，强调合成器的冷峻质感；影像段落则转向原声乐器，构筑更亲密的氛围。专辑在法国西端的乌尚岛录制，五首作品时长紧凑，其中单曲《Lena》以缓慢移动的合成器铺垫情绪，远处人声层层叠加。整体制作兼具声音探索与叙事功能，体现了剧场音乐特有的空间感与戏剧张力。

items.body: Black Lotus, the project of artist Thai, is releasing a concept EP titled “In a Room Full of Dreams” through dark synthwave, dark synth-pop, darkwave and related electronic sounds built around synesthesia, dreams, memory and perception. The title track arrives on 14 September 2026. A streaming link for the title track itself was not confirmed at the time of writing. The EP follows the earlier single “Dreams of Snakes“, already available on Spotify, and includes the tracks “When Sound Becomes Colour” and “Synthesia” alongside the title track. Geert Coppens joins Black Lotus on ‘Dreams of Snakes’ Belgian musician Geert Coppens performs as a vocal duo with Thai on “Dreams of Snakes” and has also contributed to the EP’s visual and video work. Coppens’ back-catalogue reaches into Belgium’s early minimal wave, darkwave and coldwave scenes. About Black Lotus and Geert Coppens Geert Coppens is a Belgian musician who co-founded the Micrart Group with classmate Peter Bonne in 1977, and the two went on to form the new wave band Autumn, active from 1980 to 1984. In 1982, while still working within Autumn, Coppens and Bonne began Twilight Ritual as a side project exploring a darker, more minimal sound; the pair kept Twilight Ritual a two-person project until their paths split in 1985, when Bonne went on to form A Split Second with Marc Ickx while Coppens continued designing artwork for that project and kept working under the Micrart banner. Autumn material was later compiled by Minimal Wave Records on the “Synthesize” collection, and Twilight Ritual has since been reissued on Genetic Music, Onderstroom Records and Wave Records, whose 2021 compilation “1982-2021” gathered 34 tracks spanning the project’s full history. Coppens has also worked more recently under the name Das Cabinett and, in 2023, teamed with Miami-based artist Nina Belief on the EP “In Memory Of” as Faceless 50. His appearance on “Dreams of Snakes” extends that history of collaboration into Black Lotus’s “In a Room Full of Dreams”. Black Lotus is the project of artist Thai, working across music, dance, photography, video, installation and performance-based visual art. “In a Room Full of Dreams” continues that multidisciplinary approach, pairing the EP’s concept around synesthesia and altered perception with Coppens’ contributions to both the music and the accompanying visuals.
items._cn_summary: Black Lotus 是一由艺术家 Thai 主导的多媒体项目，新作以联觉、梦境、记忆与感知为核心概念，邀请比利时资深音乐人 Geert Coppens 跨刀合作。整张 EP 横跨暗合成波、暗合成流行与暗潮等电子领域，声音与视觉围绕知觉错位展开统一构思。Coppens 在单曲《Dreams of Snakes》中以双人演唱形式参与，并为 EP 提供视觉与影像创作，其早年参与比利时极简波与冷潮运动的背景为作品带来历史厚度。Thai 本身横跨音乐、舞蹈、摄影、影像、装置与行为艺术，将听觉作品延展为跨媒介体验。EP 收录四首曲目，但原文为新专辑预告性质，缺乏对实际声音细节与制作水准的深入评论，信息有限。

items.body:
A debut, digital-only EP from a Danish trio, led by one of the Nordic folk scene�s outstanding and experienced vocalists, Mia Guldhammer. Five tracks, with the musicians bringing their own perspectives to mostly traditional music. There�s a lovely ancient, creaky mood throughout.
The opener, �Svennedal,� with its rough, cantering rhythm, offers a perfect shop window for Guldhammer�s impressive, persuasive voice, while jaw harp and bagpipes bring an insistent propulsion to �Nordg�rd,� the only original here, by band member Morten Musicus.
Cimbalom adds a delicate backdrop to the traditional �Agnete Of Bjergmanden,� with Guldhammer�s soft jaw harp offering extra textures to the other instruments, as it brings a springy opening to the final cut, �Orms�,� mingling with flute and strings to create something quite thrilling and off kilter on this instrumental.
Five tracks, and an introduction to a band that already seems very mature and accomplished. A strong beginning � what will GuldGanger do with an entire album?

items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自丹麦三人组合的首张数字EP，共五首曲目。领唱Mia Guldhammer作为北欧民谣圈的资深人声，展现出颇具说服力的嗓音表现。作品以传统音乐为底色，成员带来各自的演奏视角。开场曲以粗犷奔腾的节奏铺陈，中段使用口簧和风笛推进原创作品，唯一原创曲目由乐队成员Morten Musicus贡献。扬琴在传统曲目中铺设细腻背景，口簧与长笛、弦乐交织于终曲，营造出不安分却令人兴奋的器乐篇章。整体弥漫着古老而略带粗粝的氛围，乐队虽初登场却显示出超越新人的成熟度，将传统北欧民谣乐器与现代编配意识相融合，展现出可期的创作潜力。

items.body: Review by BrufordFreak — The Bardic Depths are back with Peter Jones contributing as a full member (one of my favorite collaborations that he's done). This is their fourth studio album release of this decade. 1. "Islands" (8:37) excellent and fresh feeling music based on NeoProg sound palette and stylings. I really like the construct, feel, and flow of this song though it does lag a bit in places. (18.333/20)2. "Fallen Leaves" (3:03) GENESISian 12-string-with-organ and anachronistic melody lines open this as harmonized vocal "doo-doo-doo" lines become woven within the instrumental weave. As this pattern continues--throughout the entire song--I find myself rather surprised--and delighted. It's a really cool and fairly inventive (if �tude-like) piece. (8.875/10)3. "Arribabok" (4:48) borrowing a lot from George Harrison/The Beatles' Indian-influenced soundscapes (which were later further developed by the likes of Daevid Allen with his GONG and other projects as well as Steve Hillage and even Peter Gabriel and David Torn). I love Gareth Gole's Torn-Hillage-like guitar tone and play in the third minute. The vocal and congestion and crescendo at the end of the third minute reminds me of both Peter Gabriel's world music and Karl Jenkins' ADIEMUS music. Nice sax play by Peter in the fourth minute and then a nice d�nouement and return to the original palette in the final minute. (9.125/10)4. "October Sun" (8:12) More excellent vocal-centric NeoProg music that reminds me of the fine fare of both FISH ON FRIDAY and TONY PATTERSON (as well as Dave Longdon-era BIG BIG TRAIN). Though the song construct and instrumental play is rather simple and sedate, the bass and vocal work is quite excellent. I understand how solid, comforting "bedding" of easy-to-digest music can serve as an excellent foundation for the exploration/expression of more sincere ideas above it--and this does happen in this song's second half--and I understand the talent and skill it takes to render such a "bedding"--so I am not as critical of this habit or tendency as I used to be (always looking for the sophistication and instrumental virtuosity in each song). I actually really appreciate the way the band has constructed and rendered this song. (17.75/20)5. "From Empty Trees" (4:41) an instrumental opening that sounds like something Tony Banks would have done for Genesis (or himself?) back in the breakout period of the band's popularity. Gareth's guitar work in his lead time during the third minute is okay but nothing very innovative--and the ascending four-chord motif that follows feels so much like Tom Johnson's "Uncertain Smile" ending jam from his 1983 The The album, Soul Mining (with that amazing piano solo from Jools Holland). (8.75/10)6. "A View" (6:18) a gorgeous NeoGenesis weave of arpeggiating keyboard and acoustic and electric guitars with solid low end support from well-coordinated bass and drums also sees some excellent synth strings orchestra and old Mellotron threads in the weave as Peter sings with his usual folk-bard-like approach. Nice weave of multiple other guitar and keyboard lines topped off by a nice heavily-reverbed sax solo from Peter in the fourth minute which is then followed by a fine electric guitar solo. Peter's voice and vocal styling is so classic, so powerful, so iconic. It's no wonder he's been the vocalist of so many 21st Century NeoProg classics. (8.875/10)7. "Harder to See" (4:09) a little more sophistication, syncopation, and frequent key changing makes this an interesting tune--especially when attending to Peter's vocal (he's got to be spot on for this one!) Once the pattern of the four chord motif is established (almost Van Morrison "Moondance"-like), the music becomes more familiar and, thus, comfortable. The chorus and follow-up d�nouement and fade out come easily but are not quite the finish one might hope for. (8.875/10)8. "Rewind" (9:21) this one opens up as another acoustic guitar- and piano-dominated weave that incorporates a four-way vocal approach, lead and harmonies, reminding me of MOON SAFARI as well as bands like Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young or even Wobbler and The Beach Boys. Nice instrumental work in the instrumental section from the third minute to the fifth and then again after 4:40 when things switch to a more ambient/atmospheric palette. (Who's playing the flutes?) This is very psychedelic in its pastoral dream-like feel--very similar to some of Steve Hackett's best stuff ("Cinema Show," Wind and Wuthering, and his early solo albums). Interesting that the the rest of the song (and album) plays out with this atmospheric instrumental weave--five minutes of it (not unlike that odd prolonged ending to "Dancing with the Moonlight Knight")! Luckily, it's really nice! The boys are obviously serious students of the masterpieces of prog's Golden Age. (18.5/20)Total Time 49:09The band's NeoProg music has continued to develop, progressing into more sophisticated and original realms of prog--that remind me of both Peter Gabriel and Fish On Fridays. With any lineup that includes prog-savant Peter Jones one cannot help but have high expectations. The problem comes with the frequent disappointments that come with the feelings of "underdeveloped," "not fully-realized" or "falling short" of possible potentialities. B+/4.5 stars; an excellent album of creative, top-notch NeoProg from some of England's most reverential and proficient veterans. Highly recommended--especially if you like the NeoProg sub-genre where it might be considered an essential masterpiece.

items.body: Spanish producer Nightcrawler releases the single “Reactor 4” on September 17, 2026, the first track from his forthcoming album “Uranium 235” on Nightcrawler Music. An official video accompanies the release. “Reactor 4” mixes dark techno, industrial electronics and cinematic textures. The single and its video take their titles from nuclear engineering, and Nightcrawler describes the video as the first look into the album’s dystopian universe, setting up “Uranium 235” as a concept record built around that imagery. The track was produced, mixed and mastered at NC Sound Studio, Nightcrawler’s own studio. Nightcrawler also directed the video, and cover design comes from George Gold Design, which also created the artwork for the 2025 Nightcrawler and Spammerheads collaboration “Ghostless”. “Reactor 4” arrives on all digital platforms and Bandcamp from September 17. About Nightcrawler Nightcrawler is a Spanish electronic music project active since 2011, built around horror and sci-fi film scores and a mix of dark atmospheres with driving electronic rhythms. The project released the “Strange Shadows” EP in 2014 and built out an extensive Bandcamp catalogue since, including releases such as “Visionary”, “Metropolis” and the “Corrupted System” and “R.U.S.H.” singles. In April 2025, Nightcrawler teamed up with the Valencia-based EBM duo Spammerheads for the collaborative single “Ghostless”, which Side-Line covered at the time. On November 13, 2025, Nightcrawler released the album “Malevolent Forces” through Nightcrawler Music, an eight-track record built on film-inspired EBM and spoken-word samples that Side-Line reviewed. “Reactor 4”, out September 17, 2026, is the first single from the project’s next album, “Uranium 235”. Nightcrawler continues to release music independently through Nightcrawler Music.

items.body: Sebastian R. Komor has launched a new project, SRK Group, with the single “Spitfire”, released September 11, 2026 on Infacted Recordings. The Polish-born, Norwegian-raised, Canada-based producer is best known as a longtime member of Icon of Coil. “Spitfire” combines dark electro, EBM and club-oriented electronics. Komor wrote, mixed and produced the track himself at his Xenomorph Productions studio; mastering is also credited to Xenomorph Productions. Describing the song, Komor calls it “personal, loud and danceable.” Spitfire by SRK Group “Spitfire” is available now on Bandcamp and streaming services. About Sebastian Komor Sebastian R. Komor was born in Zabrze, Poland, on May 7, 1976, and moved to Norway in 1981, where he grew up in Fredrikstad’s EBM and industrial scene alongside acts such as Apoptygma Berzerk. He released his first demo in 1992 and recorded under names including Melt, Area51, Sector9 and Moonitor before teaming up with fellow Fredrikstad musician Andy LaPlegua. That collaboration led to the formation of Icon of Coil in 1997; Komor became a full member during the production of the debut single “Shallow Nation” in 2000 and went on to co-write the albums “Serenity Is the Devil” (2000), “The Soul Is in the Software” (2002) and “Machines Are Us” (2004). Komor relocated to Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, in 2004. The following year he started Zombie Girl with Renee Cooper, releasing an EP in 2006 and the album “Back From the Dead” on Alfa Matrix and Metropolis Records in 2007. He later signed to FiXT for the solo hard techno and industrial project Squarehead, released the techno/tribal album “To the Past From the Future in the Present” as Moonitor, and continued his dark techno and EBM alias Komor Kommando, whose releases include the “One By One” EP on Alfa Matrix in 2022. Beyond his own projects, Komor built an extensive catalogue as a producer, mixer and mastering engineer, working with artists including Apoptygma Berzerk, Front Line Assembly, Ayria, Covenant, Circle of Dust and The True Union. His project Bruderschaft brought him together with Ronan Harris of VNV Nation, Joakim Montelius of Covenant, and Stephan Groth of Apoptygma Berzerk. SRK Group, launched with “Spitfire” on Infacted Recordings, is his newest outlet after roughly three decades in the electronic underground.

items.body: Kansas City post-punk duo Redder Moon have released an official video for “If You’re Falling, Dive”, the title track of their 2025 album of the same name. The album, eight tracks of gothic new wave and dark wave post-punk, was released August 28, 2025, and was mastered by Gordy Goudie, known for his work with Simple Minds and Echo & The Bunnymen. Redder Moon is Jeremiah James Gonzales, who writes the songs and sings, and touring bassist Sergio Anthony Gonzales-Gonzalez. The video for “If You’re Falling, Dive” sets shadow play and shifting lights against hand-drawn animation and shifting silhouettes, with Gonzales’s baritone vocal running through swirling synths and layered guitars. Gonzales described the song as “a meditation on mortality, identity, and the unseen paths our lives might have taken,” adding that it explores “the temptation to compare ourselves with who we could have been” and that “what begins as chaos can become transformation.” If You’re Falling, Dive by Redder Moon The video arrives as Redder Moon prepare for a fall 2026 tour through the American southeast, midwest and southwest. The duo have previously toured with Nite, Matte Blvck, Dead On A Sunday, Vision Video and Rosegarden Funeral Party, acts whose sound sits alongside Redder Moon’s own mix of post-punk gloom and early-’90s Depeche Mode-indebted synth work. “If You’re Falling, Dive” is available now on Bandcamp and streaming services. About Redder Moon Redder Moon is a gothic new wave and post-punk project from Kansas City, Missouri, built around analog synths, dark dance beats and dreamy guitars. The current lineup, formed in 2024, pairs songwriter and vocalist Jeremiah James Gonzales with touring bassist Sergio Anthony Gonzales-Gonzalez; the two are cousins of Mexican American, Latin heritage. The band released a run of singles and albums on Bandcamp, including “She Was Certainly Bit By Something,” “Land of the Blind” and “Hell is Other People,” building a following through the Kansas City post-punk and goth scene, including a live performance at Minibar in Kansas City in November 2024. Redder Moon’s most recent full-length, “If You’re Falling, Dive,” followed in August 2025, mastered by Gordy Goudie. Singles from the record, including “No One Lives Forever,” “Current Heartbeat,” “Someone’s Going To Cry” and “Endless Lullaby,” each arrived with their own videos. The band has toured extensively alongside Nite, Matte Blvck, Dead On A Sunday, Vision Video and Rosegarden Funeral Party, and the new video for the album’s title track lands as the group heads into a fall 2026 tour of the American southeast, midwest and southwest.

items.album: Dark Pop Artist Midniter Puts Longing Into Motion in Video for “I Could Love You”

items.body: Don’t you know I could love you better Be your release when you’re under pressure All that you hold, we could hold together I could be, I would be if you let me Somewhere inside I Could Love You is a person pacing around a room, rehearsing the case for why somebody ought to love them back. Every argument has already been prepared: I understand you, I can carry some of this weight, I can protect you, I can give you something better. None of it changes the verdict. With this new single, Midniter takes us somewhere between genuine tenderness and the dangerous confidence of believing you know what another person needs. Nic Pugh sings it without burying himself beneath theatrical anguish. The melody keeps drawing him toward the same impossible proposition, while piano and synthesizers give the track a strange openness, almost too much room for these thoughts to wander around unchecked. You can hear why Pugh calls it a ballad, although its emotional center feels closer to fixation slowly becoming aware of itself. “I Could Love You came from an old piano tune that I never finished,” Pugh reflects. “The bookends of the song are directly from that idea, with the middle evolving into a more synthpop direction for Midniter. To me, it’s a pretty standard ballad about unrequited love – a tale as old as time that everyone can understand.” The interesting part is how quickly “I could love you” changes meaning when repeated often enough. At first it sounds generous. Later it begins carrying frustration, entitlement, bargaining, hope, and the awful knowledge that intimacy cannot be argued into existence. Pugh keeps returning to the same emotional doorstep because leaving would require admitting that closeness has limits, and that another person can feel affection without crossing the line you desperately want erased. The video carries on this uncertainty, and wisely leaves plenty unexplained. Dustie Bayer moves through quiet Charlotte locations while dancers Audrey Baran, Faith Centa, and Donovan Granville turn physical proximity into something unstable. Bodies meet, separate, lean toward one another, then occupy their own space again. Pugh appears with Joe Boyland and Dan Hitzelberger behind a backlit white bedsheet, reduced to silhouettes, as though desire itself has flattened everyone involved into shapes onto which meaning can be projected. “The video is more ambiguous, playing with the question, ‘Is this about desire, obsession, or both?’ It’s ultimately your call to make. Our goal with this video was to focus more on mood than narrative. It was more important to live in these feelings of distance and longing than explain why they linger. The dancers, our friends from Baran Dance, were instrumental in carrying those moods throughout the video with their choreography. Our main actress Dustie Bayer was also incredible in her debut.” Watch below: Loving somebody from afar can feel noble when told from inside your own head. Midniter lets enough doubt creep into the room to make that certainty increasingly difficult to trust. I Could Love You is out now, coinciding with the launch of vinyl LP pre-orders for Xeno through SugarTank! Records’ new website. Xeno will be released on 27 October 2026. items.body: Review by arcane-beautiful — A different step in direction for the band after a few line up changes and a period of inactivity, the band came back with a completely different vibe, but with familiar technical speeds and playing. The attempt at moving into a more progressive sound that they tried on Scruillous is more fully felt on this album, with vocalist Rody Walker almost sounding like a different singer, with a cleaner and less punky sound to his voice. At times his range does show some weakness, but the overall passion on this album from him and the rest of the band is very potent. Lyrically being a concept album based on American exceptionalism, it is very well crafted. The track I'd recommend is From The Sky.

items.body: Review by alainPP — Side 1 opens with "Do What U Will," a surprising electro-gothic track?echoes of Ultravox with vocals reminiscent of Alice Cooper. A welcome return to contemporary rock after a six-year hiatus. "Hey Humanity" returns to a signature sound, with faint traces of Bowie and the Beatles. Colorful keyboards meet a Led Zeppelin-esque vibe?a Xavier trademark?alongside a desire to soar on symphonic elements reminiscent of ELO and sparkling guitar work. A vibrant finale featuring Queen-style guitar?magnificent, yet all too brief. "Driving To Destruction" features percussive piano � la Sheller, staccato drums, and melancholic, U2-esque guitars. It's all here: a dash of XTC and ELO, backing vocals, Supertramp-style piano, Rogue Male-style guitar, and distinctive vocal phrasing. The dynamic lyrics hint at a crash far more serious than it initially appears. "Stay With Me" follows, with vocals melting into a haughty melody amidst a blend of synth pads and keyboards. The lyrics suggest a call to action?rolling up one's sleeves to save Gaia?delivered with a Beatles-esque, crossover sound. Then comes "Charlie Knew," echoing the great Lou Reed; an epic, operatic track with symphonic orchestration. It offers a somber reflection on the times as they descend into darkness, featuring a vintage Bowie vibe and a soaring, lyrical passage that channels Cooper's madness and ELO's hope?a concentrated dose of prog.Side B opens with "Siren In The Storm," an acoustic Western-style ballad played by Kaitlin?a song of being lost amidst the waves. Captivating, narrative vocals tell the story of a siren meant to save the hero; Savannah's moving voice evokes *The Dark Side of the Moon* before a melancholic solo launches "Enigmatic Terminus." That track takes flight with sharp violins, languid vocals, and radiant, U2-style electric guitar. It is a dark, metallic tale of an approaching end, driven by a linear, martial rhythm. "Legend of Mary Jo" is a charismatic track?an old-fashioned tune with an epic, old-world duration. It tells a sad, sordid tale of love in which the heroine stays with her unfaithful husband?a parable for our own disheartened society. Originally written early in his career while playing with The Sun Machine, it is a conceptual piece?reminiscent of the Beatles and Alice Cooper?featuring classical instruments and trumpets. It has a jovial, vibrant feel?I'm sticking with the Sparks-like synth comparison?alongside a colorful, Supertramp-esque saxophone drift and a soaring, Pink Floyd-style atmosphere; a gravelly vocal cuts through a choppy, Yes-style riff and its rock-oriented variations. It boasts a distinctive sound and a solemn finale that evokes the woman's incredible destiny. A track worthy of the prog giants, featuring a blissful, final Mellotron flourish.Phideaux returns, taking his time?true to his fundamental approach. It is an epic journey best experienced in the car?a blend of psychedelic folk and progressive rock that reveals itself to be far more complex and intricate than it initially seems.

items._cn_summary: Phideaux 沉寂六年后推出双面专辑《AutoMoto Animus》，延续其标志性的折衷主义创作路径。A面以电子哥特元素开篇，随后回到乐队拿手的交响前卫路线，融合齐柏林飞艇式的律动、ELO的键盘色彩与Queen式的吉他爆发，歌词暗藏对现代社会的批判。B面更趋叙事化与器乐驱动，西部民谣小品与宏大史诗交织，小提琴与铜管被引入，Pink Floyd式氛围与Yes式摇滚变奏交替推进。整体编排密集，引用大量经典摇滚参照系，但更倾向于致敬式的拼贴而非真正意义上的声音实验。对于偏好前沿实验与前卫即兴的听众而言，这张作品扎根于上世纪七十年代摇滚语法，融合姿态保守，革新空间有限。

items.body: Review by Prog Dog — This is a mellow, lush-sounding melodic rock instrumental album, with flashes of fusion and ambient textures around the edges. The band deliberately went for a distinctly "human" sound, avoiding excessive editing and resisting the urge to snap everything onto an electronic grid. In an age of compulsive digital perfection, there's something refreshing about leaving a little room for spontaneity?and even imperfection.Overall, this is a meditative album, ideally suited to enjoying while orbiting the Earth on a space station. There are a few moments with a jazz-fusion feel, including a track featuring electric violin, but for the most part the music inhabits its own spacious, melodic world. At times I was reminded of the solo work of Steve Howe and Steve Hackett, along with Robert Fripp, Pink Floyd, and even Pattern-Seeking Animals. But the further I got into Paradigms 2, the less useful those comparisons became. TAP seem to be defining a sound of their own.It's a little less edgy than their first album, Paradigms, but Paradigms 2 is more expansive and refined, with a broader and more varied sonic palette. It feels like a natural progression from TAP's debut, and a welcome addition to the growing body of work from this geographically separated partnership of musicians working across the USA, Canada, and England.The musicians (including several guests) are a treat throughout the album, bringing a diverse range of textures to the music. UK guitarist Suzi James (Fearful Symmetry) delivers flowing solos?sometimes with an Holdsworth-inspired flavour?along with some suitably proggy slide guitar. Texas-based Mark Cook adds the distinctive sound of the Warr guitar, mostly played fretless in the bass role. Together, they provide Paradigms 2 with plenty of instrumental colour without overwhelming its relaxed, atmospheric character.Key to the album's framework and beginnings, though, were the keyboard-based compositions Michael Jobborn sent out to the rest of the band. In a somewhat backwards fashion, the musicians took the pieces from there, massaging and developing them while gradually adding their own layers and contributions. This includes the competent and detailed drum work of Bill Bachman?whose grandfather, incidentally, was involved in the invention of the 33⅓ RPM LP.A couple of the tracks take a while to fully find themselves, including "A Hole in the Ground," although it has become one of my favourites on the album. It also features some surprisingly gentle vocals?a first for the band, although apparently not something they intend to make a regular feature.My one reservation is that Paradigms II could perhaps use a little more grit and sandpapery roughness to stretch its dynamics just a touch further. Whether that comes down to the compositions, recording, mixing, mastering, or some combination of all four, I'm not sure. I certainly can't fault the band for the achievement of putting this together largely as a home-studio project, if I have my facts straight. There's plenty here to admire. "4th Dimensional Wave" and the guitar solo work in "Wishful Solitude" provide a glimpse of what this kind of edge brings to the overall sound, adding even more texture and contrast to this spacious landscape.I can also attest that this album is a grower; the more I listened, the more it revealed itself.Overall: Paradigms II is a thoughtful, atmospheric progression from TAP's debut?an album that rewards relaxed listening and, preferably, a little distance out in Earth's orbit.4.25 out of 5 dog bones- or 4 out of 5 stars for the progarchives system.

items.body: Lords Of Acid release “Ich Will Nur Das” (I Just Want) on Metropolis Records on 11 September 2026, the group’s fourth single of the year. The frenetic dance track features a vocal by US electronic musician Mari Kattman, sung entirely in German. Ich Will Nur Das by Lords Of Acid Lords Of Acid founder Praga Khan describes the track as “basically a love song with a serious identity crisis. The verses are pure lust: hot, dirty, aggressive and completely unapologetic. Then the chorus suddenly turns into the romantic fantasy of a lovestruck teenager dreaming about eternal love.” Kattman is a Metropolis Records labelmate and a non-German speaker who has been touring on her own recent solo album, “Year Of The Katt.” “She was perfect for this song, as it is incredibly charming to hear her American voice attack these German lyrics,” Khan said. “We didn’t want her pronunciation to be too polished or perfect, as her accent gives the track extra personality. She also understood the contradiction at the heart of the song: one minute she sounds like she wants to devour you, the next she’s dreaming about everlasting love. It’s filthy and innocent at the same time, which is pretty much Lords Of Acid in a nutshell.” “Ich Will Nur Das” follows the previously released “Karaoke Superstar” featuring Princess Superstar, “Dream Boy” featuring Carla Harvey, and “El Mundo Esta Loco” featuring Tony & The Kiki. All four songs appear on “Mundo Bizarro,” the group’s new album, which streams digitally from 15 October to coincide with part two of the “Cheeky Freaky” US tour, with LP and CD editions following on 6 November. “Mundo Bizarro” tracklist: “Dream Boy,” “Dancing On The Flames,” “El Mundo Esta Loco,” “Dopamine War,” “Maximo Roboto,” “Ich Will Nur Das,” “City Of Angels,” “So Stoned Today,” “Karaoke Superstar,” “You’re Obscene” and “A Viking’s Heart.” About Lords Of Acid Lords Of Acid formed in Antwerp, Belgium in 1988 around Praga Khan and are recognised as one of the most influential acts to emerge from the hard-edged electronic dance music scene of that era, blending techno, acid house and industrial music with lyrics on sexuality, drug use and hedonism. The group debuted with the New Beat single “I Sit On Acid,” and its debut album “Lust” appeared in 1991, followed by further releases that saw the band become a staple of the Billboard dance and alternative charts. Carla Harvey, formerly of Butcher Babies, joined as singer in 2025. Having built a global following across a multi-decade touring career, Lords Of Acid remain one of the genre’s most recognisable names, with “Ich Will Nur Das” arriving ahead of the group’s next album, “Mundo Bizarro,” streaming digitally from 15 October 2026 ahead of LP and CD editions on 6 November.
items._cn_summary: 比利时电子团体 Lords Of Acid 即将在 Metropolis Records 发行全德语单曲《Ich Will Nur Das》，由美国电子音乐人 Mari Kattman 演唱整首德语歌词，其美式口音成为这首歌的特色之一。制作人 Praga Khan 将这首歌描述为"带有严重身份危机的情歌"——主歌部分是纯粹的情欲表达，激烈、肮脏且毫不掩饰，而副歌部分突然转向浪漫幻想。Kattman 的非母语发音被刻意保留，以增添个性。新专辑《Mundo Bizarro》将收录此前发行的四首单曲以及多首新作，数字版于10月上线，实体版于11月发行。这是乐队2025年新主唱 Carla Harvey 加入后的延续作品，整体延续了乐队自1988年以来在techno、acid house与工业音乐领域的融合路线。

items.body: Cold Spring hosts a label night at The Globe in Glossop on 3 October 2026, with T.A.G.C., Satori, Colossloth and Llyn Y Cwn performing alongside a Cold Spring stall. Doors run from 7pm to 10:30pm, with tickets available through Resident Advisor and the event’s Facebook page. T.A.G.C. (The Anti Group Communications) was devised by Adi Newton and Steven James Turner in 1978 as a multi-dimensional research and development project. Newton uses T.A.G.C. as an outlet for his research into psycho-acoustic music, built from carefully constructed aural rituals. He is also the driving force behind Clock DVA, The Anti Group and The Future, the pre-Human League project, and a key figure in the development of electronic, industrial and experimental music since the late 1970s. T.A.G.C.’s “Iso-Erotic Calibration” is out now on Cold Spring on CD, LP and limited LP. British industrial veterans Satori formed in 1984 and have released material on cult labels including Broken Flag, Mindscan, Cold Spring and Tesco Organisation. The Glossop date doubles as the launch for Satori’s new album, “Your Life Is Worth Nothing,” which pairs harsh noise and power electronics with heavier percussive beats than the act’s earlier material. Colossloth, from the Midlands, marks 20 years as a project in 2026 and launches the new album “The Transformation And Resolution Of All Opposites” at the Glossop show. Colossloth’s music moves between brooding, abrasive passages and more transcendental material, drawing on industrial, ethnic tribalism and rave influences. Llyn Y Cwn is the solo project of Ben Powell, who has made electronic music for over 25 years, drawing on the landscapes of North Wales and his experience on Arctic research cruises. He presents “Megaliths In Dub” versus “Aniara” as an exclusive first listen at the Glossop show. About Cold Spring Cold Spring is a British independent record label focused on industrial, power electronics, noise, dark ambient and experimental music. The label has released material from artists including T.A.G.C., Satori and Colossloth, and has previously staged label nights and compilations such as the “Arise – A Cold Spring Sampler” collection. The Glossop show brings together acts from across the label’s roster, including two new album launches from Satori and Colossloth, alongside a live set from Clock DVA and Human League co-founder Adi Newton under his T.A.G.C. name.

items.body: 東京都交響楽団第1049回定期演奏会Aシリーズ Tokyo Metropolitan Symphony Orchestra Subscription Concert No.1049 A Series 2026年8月8日 東京芸術劇場 2026/8/8 Tokyo Metropolitan Theatre Reviewed by 齋藤俊夫(Toshio Saito) Photos by (c)Rikimaru Hotta／提供：東京都交響楽団 <演奏> 指揮：尾高忠明 ピアノ：北村朋幹(*) コンサートマスター：山本友重 東京都交響楽団 <曲目> 三善晃：オーケストラのための『ノエシス』 松村禎三：『ピアノ協奏曲第2番』(*) エルガー：『エニグマ変奏曲』   “無”と書いた軸を掛けても、何もなくなりません。“死”と書いた軸の場合は、何もかもなくなる。“無”ではなくならん。“死”ではなくなる！ 井上靖『本覺坊遺文』より 本公演の前半2曲、三善晃『ノエシス』と松村禎三『ピアノ協奏曲第2番』に深く刻み込まれているのは、人間がそこから逃れることのできない「死」という事象であった。 6分ほどのごく短い作品ながら、三善の音楽の全ての要素が含まれていると言っても過言ではない『ノエシス』の、雷神か怨霊が乱れ狂い歌い狂うような音響に続く後奏の静けさ。その静けさを構成するのは、「死」だ。いや、乱れ歌う音響もまた「死」の体験を延長したものなのかもしれない。なんと苛烈な世界で三善は生きてきたのか。苛烈な世界で「死」を忘れることなく想いつつ、生き抜いた彼の美的倫理……ああ、過酷だ。あまりにも過酷すぎる。 松村禎三『ピアノ協奏曲第2番』、これもまた苛烈な音楽であった。松村の原体験に結核での長い療養生活があることは周知の事実だが、その生と死が紙一重となった体験を「凝視すること」を音楽体験に変換した「オスティナート（執拗な反復）」の楽想の恐ろしさ。師・伊福部昭の、生を肯定するたくましいオスティナートとは全く異なる、ひたすら「死とは何か」を念じ続ける強迫的なオスティナート。第1楽章序盤から結末まで、北村朋幹の澄み切ったピアノの音色が音楽に透徹した思索性を与え、またそのピアノを起点としてのオーケストラの響きを捌き切る尾高の指揮、それに応える都響の演奏、どこにも隙がない。隙がないということは松村オスティナートの強迫的音響が終始こちらの心の芯に刺さり、震わせ続けるということだ。なんたる音楽体験。 第2楽章に入り、冒頭からの静かな北村のピアノ独奏が厳しく、されど儚く、でも死を凝視する強い意志をもって。諸行無常という諦観とは無縁な、もっと力強い音楽。やがて始まるピアノのトレモロに生命力が宿り、そこからオーケストラとピアノの強靭な楽想が噴火する。これは生への意志か？ 死への意志か？ 全てをねじ伏せるような力強さ。だが最後（最期）は静寂の中へ、死へと落ちゆく。全てはそこに帰す、という厳然たる真実をこちらに突きつけて、終わる。 公演後半は、人類が2つの世界大戦を経験する以前のいわゆる「クラシック音楽」であるエルガー『エニグマ変奏曲』の美しさを、エルガーの世界的権威尾高忠明の指揮で聴くというなんとも贅沢なプログラムであった。 最初に憂いを帯びた主題が提示される時点で「あー、クラシック音楽は綺麗だ」とうっとりとさせられる。そこから典雅な第1変奏、無窮動的第2変奏、おどけた第3変奏……と進むそれぞれの音楽が実に「これでしかありえない」という確固たる構築性を持って組み立てられている。ヨーロッパの教会建築のような堂々たる荘厳かつ崇高な音楽が現前し、そこに筆者は音楽の持つ陽性な宗教的精神すら汲み取った。さらに、建築といってもガチガチに表面なや内部が固まることなく、生物的な柔軟さとしなやかさをも兼ね備えた有機的建築物である。第9変奏「ニムロッド」の優しく温かい音楽や、最終第14変奏の即興的ダイナミズムを持ちつつ完璧な構造を現実化したレアリゼなど、まさに尾高の独壇場ではないか。なんというか、「さすが世界レベルの権威だ」とぐうの音も出ないほどに心服させられた。 死を強く思わせる前半、優しく抱きしめてくれる後半、と対照的な音楽ながら、どちらも超一流の仕事を聴かせてもらった。尾高マエストロ、北村朋幹、都響、皆に心からの賛辞を。 (2026/9/15)

items.body: Label: Shift Paradigm Records, 2026 Personnel - Zeju Zheng: guitar; Arnie Sainz: piano; Drew Gress: bass; Chidiebere Emmanuel: drums. Emerging guitarist Zeju Zheng is based in New York, the city he relocated to in order to pursue a Master's Degree in Jazz Performance at New York University. Zheng, who studied under Peter Bernstein and Adam Rogers, releases his debut album, A Mind in Motion , which features six original compositions exploring themes of transition, memory, hope, and discovery. The pieces, written and recorded during Zheng's early years in New York, are performed by a quartet featuring pianist Arnie Sainz, seasoned bassist Drew Gress, and Nigerian-born drummer Chidiebere Emmanuel. " 53 " is pure post-bop sophistication in 5/4, spreading fragments of Miles and Shorter's ESP years. Invigorating tonal and rhythmic shifts, a straightforward swinging drive, and expressively patterned and articulated solos from Zheng and Sainz make this an exciting opener. “ Simple ", whose 6/8 feel creates an exciting spark, emerged from Zheng's studies with eclectic guitarist Brad Shepik. His influence transpires in the guitarist's busy yet precise solo. Before that, Sainz excels in phrasing and mood, likely spurred by Gress's decisive bass figure at the bottom. Guitar and piano unisons revisit the theme, providing a tidy resolution. Zheng showcases a balladic side on tunes like " Drain ", whose sense of calmness inspires a notable solo from Gress, and " At The Corner ", where the band plunges into a meditative melodic languor offered with a rich, rounded quality. The mellow tone speaks directly to the album's themes, and in both pieces, Gress and Emmanuel fulfill their foundational roles with trust. Far from casting us in a dimmer light are the two final tracks: the nicely tempered " Little Song ", and the harmonically rich " Waiting For You To Be Home ", which frees the emotions while finding comfort in hope and light. Rooted in tradition yet incorporating charismatic contemporary elements, the pieces in A Mind in Motion are rendered with lithe and spry interplay. Zheng is confirmed as a name to watch in the future. Favorite Tracks: 01 - “53" ► 03 - Simple ► 06 - Waiting For You To Be Home

items.body: When I’m looking for peace and tranquillity, I head for the forest, or for the shore, or for any environment that hasn’t been completely dominated and subdued by human invention and industry. Yet when I arrive there, I’m quick to discover that this supposedly tranquil idyll is anything but; instead, it’s a constantly changing world of sound, movement, light, smells, and weather. Strangely, this tumult doesn’t stop me from finding the peace I’m looking for — in fact, it often seems a necessary condition for it. I can take hold of a moment — the colour of a leaf, the smell of damp soil — knowing that its sudden intensity will soon give way to something else, to boredom and to the next unfolding experience. I sometimes come across this apparent paradox in music, too: in order to truly savour a moment (a timbre, a harmonic colour), I have to accept that it’s only a moment (rhythm, structure). This happy contradiction is writ large across Sarah Louise’s new album, the twelfth in a series of solo acoustic guitar recordings from label Vin Du Select Qualitite. Louise gets stunning tones and timbres from her twelve-string guitar (Volume 12, twelve strings, geddit?), but these rich notes and chords are swept up in leaping, tumbling melodic refrains. Each note is perfectly incomplete, looking forwards to the next one to complete it. This is music as a riverine flow, a fast-moving stream sometimes stumbling over itself in its eagerness to hurry on down the hill towards the valley. Repetition is a sort of exuberance in the act of vanishing, a joy most apparent in the glimmering drive of ‘Late April’. Though this vital movement can be heard in every track on the album, it’s by far the only event happening in this densely-woven twelve-string world. The tension and anxiety of ‘Evidence of a Bear’, the sense of being watched by unseen eyes (or smelt by unseen nose), contrasts with the languid floating of ‘Floating Rhododendron’. The dark drama of ‘Scarab’ seems to come to a tragic conclusion, its storytelling replete with dramatic pauses and shifts in register. But it’s to the woods and mountains and streams that the album constantly turns, not by way of mimicry or simple evocation, but more like an aural memory of being there (even though I’ve never been there before — there being, perhaps, the Blue Ridge Mountains near Louise’s home in North Carolina, or maybe some other place that exists only in the music). In its own way, each piece offers fleeting glimpses of an unforgettable landscape, intense yet vaguely-recalled images of sun, mountains, trees: the landscape a river sees on its way down to the valley.   VDSQ Acoustic Series Volume 12 by Sarah Louise   Sarah Louise Vin Du Select Qualitite
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Sarah Louise为VDSQ厂牌录制的第十二张原声吉他独奏作品。她使用十二弦吉他创造出丰富多变的音色与和声色彩，旋律线条如溪流般奔涌而下，每一音符都指向下一个，构成一种不断展开的音乐流动。专辑中不同曲目呈现出多样的情绪对比：'Evidence of a Bear'带有紧张与被窥视的不安感，'Floating Rhododendron'则慵懒漂浮，'Scarab'充满黑暗戏剧性。虽然以原声吉他为核心，但演奏方式突破了传统民谣的局限，通过密集编织的音色层次和流动的结构营造出森林、山脉与溪流般的自然意象。作品更像是对自然景观的听觉记忆，而非简单的模仿或描绘。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. Find the artist online. Sara Serpa - Encounters and Collisions (Review) Karine Polwart- Laws of Motion (Review) Live in the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, 2025

items._genre: folk / ambient / contemporary classical / spoken word
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以人声与钢琴为核心的概念专辑，搭配精心的环境声效设计，根植于苏格兰传统。专辑源自艺术家在爱丁堡皇家植物园的驻留项目，讲述园中最古老棕榈树的故事——从其生命周期、植物学身份到最后被砍伐的意外发现。项目跨越七年的创作周期，包含专辑、舞台剧和配套书籍，歌词与音乐中反复出现的短语作为情感锚点，赋予作品呼吸感与冥想气质。钢琴演奏内敛而有分寸，人声温暖而富有同理心，将听众从旁观者变为参与者。虽然以民谣为底色，但其声景构建、跨媒介叙事和植物学主题的哲学思考使其超越了传统民谣范畴，带有当代古典与氛围音乐的特质。

items.body: Sudan Dudan is a Norwegian duo, Marit Karlberg and Anders Erik R�ine, who have released four albums over the last twenty years. On M�rke refrenger , their fifth, they are joined by Hans Hulb�kmo and Magnus Skavhaug Nergaard, contributing instrumentally and with the production. There are eight songs on the album with accompaniment principally led by acoustic guitar, augmented by fiddles, langeleik, lyre, jaws harp and more. The opening track, �Gard og grind� (�Fence and gate�) is a fine introduction to what is to come: finger-picked acoustic guitar, fiddle, bass and snare-drum played with brushes leading into the harmonized vocal, together creating an alluring sound drawing the listener in. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The mood of the album, reflected in its title which translates as �Dark Refrains,� is not always dark, but most of the material, including the title track, certainly has a reflective quality. According to the press release �the lyrics smoulder with unease about the present and the future, while looking back to the myths and riddles of the past. They speak of the earth, the sun, the moon, stars and planets, of lost brothers, quarrelling sisters, loss and grief, of the power of imagination, and of the answers to the simplest and most difficult riddles.� The lyrics of all the songs, in Norwegian, are included in the sleeve notes and while a hasty online translation can aid with some understanding, the full meanings tend to remain cryptic, but there is a sense that words and music complement each other. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan For all its dark moodiness, M�rke refrenger does have its lighter moments. �Bagatelle� recalls and reinvents the melody of a well-known French song, adding some off-kilter harmonies, while �Rulleball� is more characteristically Norwegian, employing a vocal style known as tralling in which words are replaced by a vocalization of the melody, originally used to accompany dances when no instrument was available. No translation necessary there. M�rke refrenger by Sudan Dudan The final track �Skriften p� veggen� (�the writing on the wall�) features, for the only time on the album, electric guitar. The sound is deep and twangy, shades of Duane Eddy or a David Lynch soundtrack and it works very well. All in all a fine, imaginatively conceived and beautifully produced record, available as a download or vinyl. Find the artists online. Tako Toki - Un Dimanche � Monaco (Review) GuldGanger - GuldGanger (Review)

. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / sound documentary
items._cn_summary: 这是一张采自芝加哥南区的现场录音作品，由录音师Ian Brennan在一位94岁祖母家的前廊录制。25位枪支暴力幸存者参与，年龄从17岁到67岁不等，他们分享亲身经历，有些是即兴说唱，有些是纯粹的口述。录音背景中混杂着真实的环境声——来自中途机场航线下、街区流浪狗的吠叫，没有添加任何音乐。一位老人讲述了失去两个儿子的经历，重复说着抱歉。录音当天恰逢特朗普下令向该市部署国民警卫队。这张专辑的收入将捐赠给Cure Violence Global组织。它不是传统意义上的音乐作品，而是一份关于枪支暴力、社会不公与社区创伤的听觉文献，具有田野录音与声音纪实的实验性价值。

Marking the Italian artist's second full-length release of 2026, after his collaborative LP with Batu, Exhale, came out in June, this new LP takes in seven tracks.
